ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.

### Critical syntax rules:
- **Do NOT use `#mod`** — Clingo does not support it. Use `\` instead: e.g., `(C - L) \ 2 = 0` for modulo.
- Each rule must be a valid Clingo statement: either a fact (`head.`), a rule (`head :- body.`), or a constraint (`:- body.`).
- **Do NOT write bare atoms separated by commas without a rule head or `:-`** — every line with comma-separated atoms needs a proper rule structure.
</rules>

<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>
</example_2>

% ------------------------------
%  Transformation:
%  - Find the minimal bounding rectangle of all non‑zero cells:
%    rows MR … MaxR, columns MC … MaxC.
%  - The colour that appears on any non‑zero border cell of that rectangle
%    becomes the colour for all interior (non‑border) cells.
%  - Interior rows are those that contain a non‑zero cell and are not the
%    top or bottom border rows. Interior columns are those that contain a
%    non‑zero cell in an interior row and are not the left border column.
%  - Output the interior (rows MR+1 … MaxR‑1, columns MC+1 … MaxC)
%    – zero cells stay 0, non‑zero cells become the border colour.
% ------------------------------

% non‑zero cells
nonzero(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.

% bounding rectangle of the non‑zero cells
minRow(MR) :- #min{R : nonzero(R,_,_)} = MR.
maxRow(MaxR) :- MaxR = #max{R : nonzero(R,_,_)}.
minCol(MC) :- #min{C : nonzero(_,C,_) } = MC.
maxCol(MaxC) :- MaxC = #max{C : nonzero(_,C,_) }.

% border cell (non‑zero and on the rectangle border)
border_cell(R,C,V) :- nonzero(R,C,V),
                    (R = MR or R = MaxR or C = MC or C = MaxC).

% choose exactly one border colour (the colour of a border cell)
1 { B : border_cell(R,C,B) } 1.

% interior rows (rows that have a non‑zero cell and are not top/bottom)
interior_row(R) :- nonzero(R,_,_), R != MR, R != MaxR.

% interior columns (columns that have a non‑zero cell in an interior row
%  and are not the left border column)
interior_col(C) :- #count{R : interior_row(R), nonzero(R,C,_)} > 0, C != MC.

% interior cell (inside the rectangle, not on the left border column)
interior(R,C,V) :- interior_row(R), interior_col(C), input(R,C,V).

% output – non‑zero interior cells become the border colour
output(Orow,Ocol,Color) :-
    interior(R,C,V),
    R = MR + 1 + Orow,
    C = MC + 1 + Ocol,
    V != 0,
    border_cell(R,C,B),
    Color = B.

% output – zero interior cells stay zero
output(Orow,Ocol,0) :-
    interior(R,C,V),
    R = MR + 1 + Orow,
    C = MC + 1 + Ocol,
    V = 0.

% exactly one colour per output position
:- output(Orow,Ocol,C1), output(Orow,Ocol,C2), C1 != C2.

% Declarations

nonzero(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.

row_nonzero(R) :- nonzero(R,_,_).
col_nonzero(C) :- nonzero(_,C,_).

minRow(MR) :- MR = #min{R : row_nonzero(R)}.
maxRow(MaxR) :- MaxR = #max{R : row_nonzero(R)}.
minCol(MC) :- MC = #min{C : col_nonzero(C)}.
maxCol(MaxC) :- MaxC = #max{C : col_nonzero(C)}.

border_cell(R,C,B) :- input(R,C,B), B != 0, R = MR, R = MaxR, C = MC, C = MaxC.

border_color_count(B,N) :- N = #count{R : border_cell(R,_,B)}.

max_border_count(M) :- M = #max{B : #count{R : border_cell(R,_,B)}}.

border_color_selected(B) :- border_cell(_,_,B), border_color_count(B,N), max_border_count(M), N = M.

% Interior cells (inside rectangle, not on border)

    interior(R,C,V),

    V = 0.

% Auxiliary facts
nonzero(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.

row_nonzero(R) :- nonzero(R,_,_).
col_nonzero(C) :- nonzero(_,C,_).

minRow(MR) :- MR = #min{R : row_nonzero(R)}.
maxRow(MaxR) :- MaxR = #max{R : row_nonzero(R)}.
minCol(MC) :- MC = #min{C : col_nonzero(C)}.
maxCol(MaxC) :- MaxC = #max{C : col_nonzero(C)}.

% Border cells (non‑zero on rectangle border)
border_cell(R,C,B) :- input(R,C,B), B != 0, R = MR, R = MaxR, C = MC, C = MaxC.

% Count border cells per color
border_color_count(B,N) :- N = #count{R : border_cell(R,_,B)}.

% Find a border color with maximal count (ties allowed)
border_color_selected(B) :- border_cell(_,_,B), border_color_count(B,N).

% Exactly one border color is chosen
1 { border_color_selected(CB) : true } 1.

% No two different colors chosen
:- border_color_selected(CB1), border_color_selected(CB2), CB1 != CB2.

% Interior cells (strictly inside rectangle)
interior(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), R != MR, R != MaxR, C != MC, C != MaxC.

% Fill output: non‑zero interior becomes border color, zero interior becomes 0
output(Orow,Ocol,C) :-
    interior(R,C,V),
    R = MR + 1 + Orow,
    C = MC + 1 + Ocol,
    V != 0,
    border_color_selected(CB),
    C = CB.

output(Orow,Ocol,0) :-
    interior(R,C,V),
    R = MR + 1 + Orow,
    C = MC + 1 + Ocol,
    V = 0.

% No two colors for same output position
:- output(Orow,Ocol,C1), output(Orow,Ocol,C2), C1 != C2.

% Auxiliary predicates
nonzero(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.

row_nonzero(R) :- nonzero(R,_,_).
col_nonzero(C) :- nonzero(_,C,_).

minRow(MR) :- MR = #min{R : row_nonzero(R)}.
maxRow(MaxR) :- MaxR = #max{R : row_nonzero(R)}.
minCol(MC) :- MC = #min{C : col_nonzero(C)}.
maxCol(MaxC) :- MaxC = #max{C : col_nonzero(C)}.

% Border cells (non‑zero on the rectangle border)
border_cell(R,C,B) :- input(R,C,B), B != 0, R = MR, R = MaxR, C = MC, C = MaxC.

% Count border cells per color
border_color_count(B,N) :- N = #count{R : border_cell(R,_,B)}.

% Choose a border color (any that appears)
border_color_selected(B) :- border_cell(_,_,B), border_color_count(B,N).

% Exactly one border color is chosen
1 { border_color_selected(CB) : true } 1.

% No two different border colors are chosen
:- border_color_selected(CB1), border_color_selected(CB2), CB1 != CB2.

% Interior cells (strictly inside the rectangle)
interior(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), R != MR, R != MaxR, C != MC, C != MaxC.

% Fill output: non‑zero interior cells become the selected border color,
% zero interior cells become 0
output(Orow,Ocol,Color) :-
    interior(R,C,V),
    R = MR + 1 + Orow,
    C = MC + 1 + Ocol,
    V != 0,
    border_color_selected(B),
    Color = B.

output(Orow,Ocol,0) :-
    interior(R,C,V),
    R = MR + 1 + Orow,
    C = MC + 1 + Ocol,
    V = 0.

% No two different colors for the same output cell
:- output(Orow,Ocol,Color1), output(Orow,Ocol,Color2), Color1 != Color2.

% Use #count for rows and columns with non-zero.

maxRow(Rmax) :- Rmax = #max{R : nonzero(R,_,_)}.
minRow(Rmin) :- Rmin = #min{R : nonzero(R,_,_)}.
maxCol(Cmax) :- Cmax = #max{C : nonzero(_,C,_) }.
minCol(Cmin) :- Cmin = #min{C : nonzero(_,C,_) }.

% Height and width
height(H) :- H = maxRow - minRow + 1.
width(W) :- W = maxCol - minCol + 1.

% Output dimensions
outRows(OrowCount) :- OrowCount = maxRow - minRow - 1.
outCols(OcolCount) :- OcolCount = maxCol - minCol - 1.

% Determine the most frequent border color
% Border cells: R = minRow or R = maxRow or C = minCol or C = maxCol, and nonzero.

border_color(B) :- nonzero(R,C,B), (R = minRow; R = maxRow; C = minCol; C = maxCol).

% Count border colors
border_count(B,N) :- border_color(B), N = #count{R : border_color(R,B)}.

% Choose a border color with maximal count (unique expected)
max_border_count(MCount) :- MCount = #max{B : border_count(B,N)}.

border_selected(B) :- border_count(B,N), max_border_count(MCount), N = MCount.

% Exactly one selected (should be unique)
1 { border_selected(CB) : true } 1.

% No other border selected color
:- border_selected(CB1), border_selected(CB2), CB1 != CB2.

% Interior cells (inside rectangle)
interior(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), R != minRow, R != maxRow, C != minCol, C != maxCol.

% Output mapping

    interior(R,C,V),
    R = minRow + 1 + Orow,
    C = minCol + 1 + Ocol,
    V != 0,
    border_selected(CB),
    Color = CB.

output(Orow,Ocol,0) :-
    interior(R,C,V),
    R = minRow + 1 + Orow,
    C = minCol + 1 + Ocol,
    V = 0.

% Enforce uniqueness per output cell

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  ARC‑AGI transformation:  
%  – find the bounding rectangle of all non‑zero cells,  
%  – the colour that appears on the (non‑zero) border of that rectangle
%    is the colour that will be written into the interior,  
%  – interior cells that are zero stay zero,  
%  – interior cells that are non‑zero become the border colour.  
%  The output grid consists of the interior part of the rectangle:
%  rows MR+1 … MaxR‑1 and columns MC+1 … MaxC‑1.
% ------------------------------------------------------------

% non‑zero cells
nonzero(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.

row_nonzero(R) :- nonzero(R,_,_).
col_nonzero(C) :- nonzero(_,C,_).

% bounding rectangle of the non‑zero cells
minRow(MR)   :- MR = #min{R : row_nonzero(R)}.
maxRow(MaxR) :- MaxR = #max{R : row_nonzero(R)}.
minCol(MC)   :- MC = #min{C : col_nonzero(C)}.
maxCol(MaxC) :- MaxC = #max{C : col_nonzero(C)}.

% border colour – a non‑zero cell that lies on the rectangle border
border_color(B) :-
    input(R,C,B), B != 0,
    R = MR, R = MaxR, C = MC, C = MaxC.

% interior cells (strictly inside the rectangle)
interior(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V),
                   R != MR, R != MaxR,
                   C != MC, C != MaxC.

% output – non‑zero interior cells become the border colour,
%           zero interior cells become 0
output(Orow,Ocol,Color) :-
    interior(R,C,V),
    R = MR + 1 + Orow,
    C = MC + 1 + Ocol,
    V != 0,
    border_color(B),
    Color = B.

output(Orow,Ocol,0) :-
    interior(R,C,V),
    R = MR + 1 + Orow,
    C = MC + 1 + Ocol,
    V = 0.

% No two different colours for the same output position
:- output(Orow,Ocol,C1), output(Orow,Ocol,C2), C1 != C2.
